card.name: Separators inside drug name lists
card.fires_on: Commas, 'and', or 'compared' that come right after a drug name and just before the next drug name in a list or comparison. Seen mostly in lists of QT-prolonging drugs, fluoroquinolones and corticosteroids.

modes.label: Comma in drug lists
modes.description: A comma after one drug name in a run of drug names.
modes.example: azine, thioridazine, chlorpromazine, droperidol, pimozide, sparfloxacin, gatifloxacin<<,>> moxifloxacin, halof

modes.label: Linking word before a drug
modes.description: 'and' or 'compared' placed between two drug names or just before a drug name in a trial comparison.

card.writes: It seems to prepare the model for another drug name to follow, and to suppress the word 'associated' and its variants.
card.plain: It marks the spot between items in a list of drug names, where another drug name is expected next.
